newsitem.title: USA: Ten Calif. localities join suit vs. BankAmerica.
newsitem.headline: Ten Calif. localities join suit vs. BankAmerica.

text.p: Ten local governments in California on Wednesday joined San Francisco and the state in suing BankAmerica Corp for allegedly mismanaging municipal bond funds.
The localities joined lawsuits filed in May by the city and county of San Francisco, and by California Attorney General Dan Lungren, according to court documents.

The lawsuits, filed in San Francisco Superior Court, alleged BankAmerica unit Bank of America overcharged issuers, failed to return unclaimed funds from bond trust accounts, and improperly invested funds from some of the accounts.
BankAmerica spokesman John Keane said "there is no new information here."
"Our response to the basic issues is the same. We believe that we have refunded any overcharges but are ready to make good on any others that can be substantiated," Keane said.
Bank of America maintains that the investments it made were appropriate, and that it has fully returned unclaimed funds from the bond accounts.

The counties of Riverside, Marin, Contra Costa, Santa Clara, Sonoma, Solano and Tulare joined the lawsuit, along with the city of Industry, the Industry Urban-Development Agency and the East Stockton Municipal Water District, according to court documents filed on Wednesday.
Asked why Contra Costa chose to join the case, Deputy County Counsel Dennis Graves said; "It looks like there's a lot of smoke here, enough that there's a pretty good fire."
The lawsuits were based on a so-called "whistleblower" complaint filed under seal in April 1995 by Patrick Stull, a former vice president for corporate trust at Bank of America.
